evidence.title: Canada's Carney and China's Xi agree to ease tariffs amid trade rows with US
evidence.body: [e001:f01] Canada's government said it had agreed to further reduce tariffs on a range of products. https:// Prefer DW on Google Carney (L) and Xi held talks ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen Image: Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen have produced deals to further reduce tariffs, Ottawa said on Tuesday. [e001:f02] The agreements reflect a growing rapprochement between the two countries after years of strained relations, thanks to trade tensions with Washington leading both Canada and China to seek to reduce dependence on the US. [e001:f03] According to a statement from the Canadian government, China is to reduce tariffs on Canadian pork, fish and seafood. [e001:f04] In exchange, Canada will prolong the current tariff exemptions for Chinese steel and aluminum for another two years. [e001:f05] The two leaders also agreed to cooperate more closely on economic and financial matters, and to work together in the fields of education and environmental protection. [e001:f06] Canada is too reliant on the United States, Carney tells DW To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Growing China-Canada rapprochement Xi and Carney already declared their intention to enhance bilateral ties during talks in Beijing in January. [e001:f07] Critics in Canada have, however, pointed out what they see as dangers to the country's security and values through the closer ties to Beijing. [e001:f08] Among other things, Canadian intelligence believes that China interfered in at least two federal elections, something Beijing denies. [e001:f09] Regardless of what comes from his talks with US President Trump, the EU will likely remain stuck between erratic US trade policy and Beijing's export machine. evidence.title: China-Canada Financial Dialogue Yields 14 Outcomes as Canadian Pension Funds Cleared to Boost Investment in Chinese Capital Markets
evidence.body: [e002:f01] Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne and International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu co-chaired the second China-Canada Economic and Financial Strategic Dialogue in Vancouver, producing 14 outcomes. [e002:f02] China welcomed long-term capital such as Canadian pension funds to invest in its capital markets through the Qualified Foreign Investor (QFI) channel, and to enter the exchange bond market directly and trade in futures products open to foreign investors. [e002:f03] The two sides also set arrangements on Panda bond issuance, RMB green sovereign bonds, drills and test use of the bilateral local-currency swap, and a financial regulatory dialogue. [e002:f04] Both sides said they would seek substantive progress in trade talks before the APEC leaders' meeting.
